NRJ-ELEC.name: Purchased electricity consumed
NRJ-ELEC.definition: Electricity purchased (grid or contract) and consumed on the site during the period. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Include: Offices, warehouses, shops, charging points located on the site. Exclude: Electricity produced and consumed on site (see NRJ-ELEC-AUTO). Source: Supplier invoices or customer account, meter readings.

NRJ-ELEC-AUTO.name: Self-generated renewable electricity consumed
NRJ-ELEC-AUTO.definition: Electricity produced on the site (solar panels, wind…) and consumed on site. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Production meter, installer's report.

NRJ-ELEC-REN.name: Purchased renewable electricity
NRJ-ELEC-REN.definition: Share of purchased electricity covered by a green tariff with guarantees of origin or by a power purchase agreement (PPA). Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Supplier certificate (guarantees of origin).

NRJ-GAZ.name: Natural gas consumed
NRJ-GAZ.definition: Natural gas consumed on the site (heating, processes, catering), in kWh GCV as on the invoices. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Supplier invoices, meter readings.

NRJ-FIOUL.name: Heating oil consumed
NRJ-FIOUL.definition: Heating oil consumed for heating or generators, in litres. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Delivery notes, tank gauging.

NRJ-CHALEUR.name: Purchased heat and steam
NRJ-CHALEUR.definition: Heat and steam purchased or received, consumed by the site: district heating network, steam from a neighbouring site, waste heat or steam received from a third party's industrial process. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Invoices of the district heating network or of the steam supplier.

NRJ-FROID.name: Purchased cooling (district cooling)
NRJ-FROID.definition: Cooling delivered by a district cooling network. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: District cooling network invoices.

CONV-FIOUL.name: Energy content of heating oil
CONV-FIOUL.definition: Energy contained in one litre of heating oil, to convert litres into kWh (about 10 kWh/L). Source: ADEME Base Empreinte or supplier.

GES-GAZOLE.name: Diesel used by vehicles
GES-GAZOLE.definition: Diesel for vehicles and machinery owned or on long-term lease by the entity. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Fuel cards, invoices.

GES-ESSENCE.name: Petrol used by vehicles
GES-ESSENCE.definition: Petrol for vehicles owned or on long-term lease by the entity. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Fuel cards, invoices.

GES-FUGITIVES.name: Fugitive emissions (refrigerants)
GES-FUGITIVES.definition: Refrigerant top-ups (air conditioning, refrigeration) multiplied by their global warming potential. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Maintenance log and refrigeration engineer's records.

FE-GAZ.name: Natural gas emission factor
FE-GAZ.definition: kgCO2e emitted per kWh GCV of natural gas burnt. Source: ADEME Base Empreinte, DEFRA, IEA or an equivalent national database; keep the same source from one year to the next.

FE-FIOUL.name: Heating oil emission factor
FE-FIOUL.definition: kgCO2e emitted per litre of heating oil burnt. Source: ADEME Base Empreinte, DEFRA, IEA or an equivalent national database; keep the same source from one year to the next.

FE-GAZOLE.name: Diesel emission factor
FE-GAZOLE.definition: kgCO2e emitted per litre of diesel. Source: ADEME Base Empreinte, DEFRA, IEA or an equivalent national database; keep the same source from one year to the next.

FE-ESSENCE.name: Petrol emission factor
FE-ESSENCE.definition: kgCO2e emitted per litre of petrol. Source: ADEME Base Empreinte, DEFRA, IEA or an equivalent national database; keep the same source from one year to the next.

FE-ELEC.name: Grid electricity emission factor (location-based)
FE-ELEC.definition: Average factor of the electricity grid in the entity's country ("location-based" method). Source: ADEME Base Empreinte, DEFRA, IEA or an equivalent national database; keep the same source from one year to the next.

FE-CHALEUR.name: Purchased heat and steam emission factor
FE-CHALEUR.definition: Factor of the heat or steam purchased by the site (district heating network, steam supplier); if the site buys both, average factor weighted by the quantities. Source: Network operator, national regulation.

FE-FROID.name: Purchased cooling emission factor
FE-FROID.definition: Factor of the district cooling network that supplies the site. Source: Network operator, national regulation.

GES-S1-FIXE.name: Stationary combustion emissions
GES-S1-FIXE.definition: Natural gas and heating oil burnt on the site, multiplied by their emission factor.

GES-S1-MOBILE.name: Mobile combustion emissions
GES-S1-MOBILE.definition: Fuels of the entity's vehicles, multiplied by their emission factor.

GES-S1.name: Scope 1: combustion and fugitive emissions (subtotal)
GES-S1.definition: Calculated subtotal: stationary and mobile combustion, and fugitive emissions. The other direct emissions (processes, other fuels, agriculture) are entered separately and added to it to make gross scope 1.

GES-S2-LB.name: Energy indirect emissions (scope 2, location-based)
GES-S2-LB.definition: Purchased electricity, heat, steam and cooling, multiplied by the average factor of their network.

GES-S3-ACHATS.name: Scope 3 – purchased goods and services (cat. 1)
GES-S3-ACHATS.definition: Emissions from the production of purchased goods and services. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-IMMO.name: Scope 3 – capital goods (cat. 2)
GES-S3-IMMO.definition: Emissions from the manufacture of equipment, buildings and vehicles acquired. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-ENERGIE.name: Scope 3 – fuel- and energy-related activities (cat. 3)
GES-S3-ENERGIE.definition: Extraction, production and transport of the energy consumed, transmission losses. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-FRET-AMONT.name: Scope 3 – upstream transportation and distribution (cat. 4)
GES-S3-FRET-AMONT.definition: Transport of purchased goods to the company's sites. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-DECHETS.name: Scope 3 – waste generated in operations (cat. 5)
GES-S3-DECHETS.definition: Treatment of the waste produced by the sites. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-DEPLACEMENTS.name: Scope 3 – business travel (cat. 6)
GES-S3-DEPLACEMENTS.definition: Trains, planes, rental cars and hotel nights for business travel. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-DOMICILE.name: Scope 3 – employee commuting (cat. 7)
GES-S3-DOMICILE.definition: Employees' journeys between their home and their workplace. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-FRET-AVAL.name: Scope 3 – downstream transportation and distribution (cat. 9)
GES-S3-FRET-AVAL.definition: Transport of sold products to customers. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-UTILISATION.name: Scope 3 – use of sold products (cat. 11)
GES-S3-UTILISATION.definition: Energy consumed by sold products during their lifetime. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-FIN-VIE.name: Scope 3 – end-of-life treatment of sold products (cat. 12)
GES-S3-FIN-VIE.definition: End-of-life treatment of sold products and their packaging. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

ECO-CA.name: Net revenue
ECO-CA.definition: Net revenue for the period, in millions of euros. Source: Consolidated accounts, management control.

SOC-EFFECTIF.name: Total headcount at end of period
SOC-EFFECTIF.definition: Employees on the payroll at the end of the period, all contracts (permanent, fixed-term, work-study), as a headcount. Exclude: Temporary agency workers, interns, contractors. Source: HR information system, payroll.

SOC-EFF-FEMMES.name: Female headcount at end of period
SOC-EFF-FEMMES.definition: Women on the payroll at the end of the period. Source: HR information system.

SOC-EFF-CDI.name: Permanent employees at end of period
SOC-EFF-CDI.definition: Employees on a permanent contract at the end of the period. Source: HR information system.

SOC-HEURES-FORM.name: Training hours
SOC-HEURES-FORM.definition: Training hours attended by employees during the period, all formats (in person, remote). Source: Skills development plan, training tool.

SOC-FORM-PAR-SAL.name: Training hours per employee
SOC-FORM-PAR-SAL.definition: Training hours divided by total headcount.

SOC-HEURES-TRAV.name: Hours worked
SOC-HEURES-TRAV.definition: Hours actually worked by employees during the period. Source: Payroll, time management.

SOC-DECES.name: Work-related fatalities
SOC-DECES.definition: Deaths of employees during the period as a result of recordable work-related accidents or recordable work-related ill health (sum of both), subject to legal restrictions. Deaths of non-employees are not counted here. Source: Health and safety department.

SOC-HANDICAP.name: Employees with disabilities
SOC-HANDICAP.definition: Employees who have declared their disability, at the end of the period. Source: HR information system.

SOC-PART-HANDICAP.name: Share of employees with disabilities
SOC-PART-HANDICAP.definition: Employees with disabilities divided by total headcount.

DEC-TOTAL.name: Total waste generated
DEC-TOTAL.definition: Waste produced by the site during the period, all streams. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Waste register, waste transfer notes and service provider reports.

DEC-DANGEREUX.name: Hazardous waste generated
DEC-DANGEREUX.definition: Share of waste classified as hazardous (oils, solvents, WEEE, batteries…). Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Hazardous waste tracking notes.

GOV-CORRUPTION.name: Convictions for corruption or bribery
GOV-CORRUPTION.definition: Final convictions for active or passive corruption handed down during the period. Source: Legal department, compliance.

GOV-AMENDES.name: Fines for corruption or bribery
GOV-AMENDES.definition: Amount of the mandatory monetary penalties imposed by a court or an administrative or regulatory authority for violation of anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws, paid to a public treasury and recognised in the financial statements of the period (Voluntary Standard VS: B11 §43 and guidance §141; ESRS G1-4 §12 and G1 AR 6, same definition). Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Accounting, legal department.

GEN-IDENT-TYPE.name: Entity identifier scheme
GEN-IDENT-TYPE.unit: list: LEI, DUNS, EU ID, PermID
GEN-IDENT-TYPE.definition: Scheme of the company's unique identifier; EFRAG recommends the LEI. Source: LEI register (GLEIF), D&B, business register.

GEN-IDENT.name: Entity identifier
GEN-IDENT.definition: Unique identifier of the company in the chosen scheme (for example the 20 characters of the LEI). Required to convert the report to XBRL.

GEN-INTRO.name: Introduction and entity-specific information
GEN-INTRO.definition: Optional introduction text of the report.

GEN-CONFORMITE.name: Explicit statement of compliance
GEN-CONFORMITE.definition: Sentence in which the company states that the report complies with the Voluntary Standard, with the module chosen.

GEN-PERIMETRE.name: Basis for reporting
GEN-PERIMETRE.unit: list: Sustainability report prepared on an individual basis, Sustainability report prepared on a consolidated basis
GEN-PERIMETRE.definition: Report prepared for the company alone (individual basis) or for the group (consolidated basis).

GEN-FORME-JURIDIQUE.name: Legal form
GEN-FORME-JURIDIQUE.unit: list: private limited liability undertaking, sole proprietorship, partnership, cooperative, other (please specify the legal form in the row below)
GEN-FORME-JURIDIQUE.definition: Legal form of the reporting company.

GEN-FORME-AUTRE.name: Legal form (if “other”)
GEN-FORME-AUTRE.definition: Only if the legal form is “Other”.

GEN-NACE.name: NACE codes of the activity
GEN-NACE.definition: NACE code(s) of the activity, one per line, written as 47.91 (the code alone is enough). Source: Business register extract.

ECO-TOTAL-BILAN.name: Balance sheet total
ECO-TOTAL-BILAN.definition: Total assets on the balance sheet at closing date, in euros. Source: Annual accounts.

GEN-CERTIF-DESC.name: Description of certifications or labels

GEN-SITE-GPS.name: GPS coordinates of the site
GEN-SITE-GPS.definition: Latitude and longitude in decimal degrees, 5 decimals, separated by a comma (e.g. 48.85661, 2.35222), as a map service gives them. The standard asks for the geolocation of each site.

GEN-FILIALES.name: List of subsidiaries
GEN-FILIALES.definition: For a report on a consolidated basis: one row per subsidiary, with its registered address. Source: Legal structure chart, consolidated accounts.

GEN-INFOS-INCHANGEES.name: Disclosures unchanged since the previous report
GEN-INFOS-INCHANGEES.definition: Optional: the disclosures that have not changed since the previous report (one per row); the link to that report is given below. Source: Previous report.

GEN-RAPPORT-LIEN.name: Link to the previous report
GEN-RAPPORT-LIEN.definition: Web address of the previous report that contains the unchanged disclosures.

GEN-OMISSIONS.name: Disclosures omitted as classified or sensitive
GEN-OMISSIONS.definition: Only if the company has omitted information because it is classified or sensitive: one row per omitted disclosure. Otherwise, leave empty. Source: Management, legal department.

GEN-COOP-PARTICIPATION.name: Cooperative: participation in governance
GEN-COOP-PARTICIPATION.definition: For a cooperative (optional EFRAG guidance): effective participation of workers, users or other parties in governance.

GEN-COOP-INVEST.name: Cooperative: investment in the social economy
GEN-COOP-INVEST.definition: Investment in the capital or assets of social economy entities (optional). Source: Accounting.

GEN-COOP-LIMITES.name: Cooperative: limits to profit distribution
GEN-COOP-LIMITES.definition: Limits to the distribution of profits linked to the mutual or general-interest nature (optional).

GOV-B2-PRATIQUES.name: Practices, policies or initiatives for the sustainable transition
GOV-B2-PRATIQUES.definition: Has the company put in place practices, policies or future initiatives for the transition towards a more sustainable economy? If yes, tick below the issues addressed.

GOV-B2-CLIMAT.name: Practices on the issue: climate change
GOV-B2-CLIMAT.definition: Does a practice, policy or initiative of the company address the issue “climate change”?

GOV-B2-POLLUTION.name: Practices on the issue: pollution
GOV-B2-POLLUTION.definition: Does a practice, policy or initiative of the company address the issue “pollution”?

GOV-B2-EAU.name: Practices on the issue: water and marine resources
GOV-B2-EAU.definition: Does a practice, policy or initiative of the company address the issue “water and marine resources”?

GOV-B2-BIODIV.name: Practices on the issue: biodiversity and ecosystems
GOV-B2-BIODIV.definition: Does a practice, policy or initiative of the company address the issue “biodiversity and ecosystems”?

GOV-B2-CIRCULAIRE.name: Practices on the issue: circular economy and resource use
GOV-B2-CIRCULAIRE.definition: Does a practice, policy or initiative of the company address the issue “circular economy and resource use”?

GOV-B2-PERSONNEL.name: Practices on the issue: own workforce
GOV-B2-PERSONNEL.definition: Does a practice, policy or initiative of the company address the issue “own workforce”?

GOV-B2-CHAINE.name: Practices on the issue: workers in the value chain
GOV-B2-CHAINE.definition: Does a practice, policy or initiative of the company address the issue “workers in the value chain”?

GOV-B2-COMMUNAUTES.name: Practices on the issue: affected communities
GOV-B2-COMMUNAUTES.definition: Does a practice, policy or initiative of the company address the issue “affected communities”?

GOV-B2-CONSO.name: Practices on the issue: consumers and end-users
GOV-B2-CONSO.definition: Does a practice, policy or initiative of the company address the issue “consumers and end-users”?

GOV-B2-CONDUITE.name: Practices on the issue: business conduct
GOV-B2-CONDUITE.definition: Does a practice, policy or initiative of the company address the issue “business conduct”?

GOV-B2-PUBLIC.name: Practice or policy publicly available
GOV-B2-PUBLIC.definition: Is at least one of these practices, policies or initiatives publicly available?

GOV-B2-CIBLE.name: Target related to a policy
GOV-B2-CIBLE.definition: Has the company set a target related to one of these policies?

NRJ-COMB-AUTRES.name: Other fossil fuels
NRJ-COMB-AUTRES.definition: Fossil fuels other than natural gas, heating oil and vehicle fuels (LPG, propane, coal, process gas), in MWh on a net calorific value basis. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Invoices, delivery notes.

NRJ-COMB-REN.name: Renewable fuels
NRJ-COMB-REN.definition: Wood, pellets, biogas, biofuels and other biomass fuels burned on the site, in MWh on a net calorific value basis. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Invoices, delivery notes.

CONV-GAZ-PCI.name: PCS du gaz naturel / Net / gross calorific value ratio of natural gas
CONV-GAZ-PCI.definition: Gas is billed in kWh of gross calorific value; the standard counts energy on a net calorific value basis. This ratio converts one into the other (about 0.901 for natural gas). Source: ADEME Base Empreinte.

CONV-GAZOLE.name: Energy content of diesel
CONV-GAZOLE.definition: Energy contained in one litre of diesel, to convert litres into kWh (about 10 kWh/L). Source: ADEME Base Empreinte or supplier.

CONV-ESSENCE.name: Energy content of petrol
CONV-ESSENCE.definition: Energy contained in one litre of petrol, to convert litres into kWh (about 9 kWh/L). Source: ADEME Base Empreinte or supplier.

NRJ-COMBUSTIBLES.name: Energy from fuels
NRJ-COMBUSTIBLES.definition: Fossil fuels: natural gas (converted to net calorific value), heating oil, vehicle fuels and other fossil fuels, in MWh.

NRJ-TOTAL-MWH.name: Total energy consumption (MWh)
NRJ-TOTAL-MWH.definition: Purchased and self-generated electricity, purchased heat, steam and cooling, fossil and renewable fuels (vehicles included), in MWh. Electricity generated on site from a fuel already counted is not added.

GES-S1-AUTRES.name: Other direct emissions (scope 1)
GES-S1-AUTRES.definition: Direct emissions not covered by the scope 1 calculation: industrial processes, other fuels (LPG, coal, biomass for CH4 and N2O), agriculture. They are added to the subtotal of combustion and fugitive emissions to make gross scope 1. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory.

GES-S2-MB.name: Energy indirect emissions (scope 2, market-based)
GES-S2-MB.definition: Scope 2 emissions calculated with the emission factors of the energy contracts: those of electricity (guarantees of origin, power purchase agreements) and also those of the purchased heat, steam and cooling given by the suppliers; for purchased energy without a contractual instrument, the residual mix factor. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory.

GES-S3-ACTIFS-AMONT.name: Scope 3 – upstream leased assets (cat. 8)
GES-S3-ACTIFS-AMONT.definition: Emissions of scope 3 category 8. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-TRANSFO.name: Scope 3 – processing of sold products (cat. 10)
GES-S3-TRANSFO.definition: Emissions of scope 3 category 10. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-ACTIFS-AVAL.name: Scope 3 – downstream leased assets (cat. 13)
GES-S3-ACTIFS-AVAL.definition: Emissions of scope 3 category 13. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-FRANCHISES.name: Scope 3 – franchises (cat. 14)
GES-S3-FRANCHISES.definition: Emissions of scope 3 category 14. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

GES-S3-INVEST.name: Scope 3 – investments (cat. 15)
GES-S3-INVEST.definition: Emissions of scope 3 category 15. A category that is not significant: answer N/A (it is not disclosed and does not count in a total). Source: Greenhouse gas emissions inventory (carbon accounting tool, service provider).

POL-DECLARATION.name: Reporting of pollutant emissions required
POL-DECLARATION.definition: Is the company already required to report its pollutant emissions to air, water or soil to the authorities (EU or national law), or does it do so in an environmental management system?

POL-PUBLIC.name: Pollutant emissions already public
POL-PUBLIC.definition: Is this information already publicly available?

POL-URL.name: Link to the published pollutant emissions
POL-URL.definition: Web address (URL) where this information is published.

POL-REJETS.name: Emissions per pollutant
POL-REJETS.unit: table: Pollutant, Emissions to air, Emissions to water, Emissions to soil
POL-REJETS.definition: If the company must already report them (or does so in an environmental management system): one row per pollutant, with its emissions to air, water and soil in kg over the period. Source: Annual emissions report, E-PRTR register.

POL-REJETS-AUTRES.name: Emissions of other pollutants
POL-REJETS-AUTRES.unit: table: Pollutant, Emissions to air, Emissions to water, Emissions to soil
POL-REJETS-AUTRES.definition: Pollutants that are not in the European list: one row per pollutant, with its name and emissions in kg. Source: Annual emissions report.

BIO-SITES.name: Sites in or near biodiversity sensitive areas
BIO-SITES.definition: Does the company have sites in or near biodiversity sensitive areas (Natura 2000, World Heritage sites, Key Biodiversity Areas)? If yes, each site concerned says so.

BIO-SITE-ZONE.name: Position of the site relative to a sensitive area
BIO-SITE-ZONE.unit: list: Located in a biodiversity sensitive area, Located near a biodiversity sensitive area, Neither in nor near a biodiversity sensitive area
BIO-SITE-ZONE.definition: Is the site in a biodiversity sensitive area, near one, or neither?

BIO-SITE-ZONE-NOM.name: Name of the sensitive area near the site
BIO-SITE-ZONE-NOM.definition: Name of the biodiversity sensitive area concerned.

EAU-PRELEVEMENT.name: Water withdrawn
EAU-PRELEVEMENT.definition: Water withdrawn by the site during the period (mains, borehole, river). Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Water bills, meter readings.

EAU-REJET-PROCESS.name: Water discharged from production processes
EAU-REJET-PROCESS.definition: Only for a site whose production processes use a lot of water (boilers, drying, washing, cooling, irrigation): water discharged by these processes. 0: no such processes. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Voluntary for a company with 10 employees or less: it can answer N/A. Source: Discharge readings, discharge permit.

EAU-STRESS.name: Water consumed at sites in water-stress areas
EAU-STRESS.definition: Water consumed by the site if it is in an area with water stress (for example a baseline water stress of ‘High’ or more in the WRI Aqueduct tool), in cubic metres: water withdrawn minus water discharged from production processes, like the water consumption of the Voluntary Standard VS (B6 §37). The ESRS have their own KPI, which deducts all discharges (E3 AR 4). Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Water bills, Aqueduct tool.

ECO-CIRCULAIRE.name: Circular economy principles applied
ECO-CIRCULAIRE.definition: Does the company apply circular economy principles (reuse, repair, recycling, eco-design)? Voluntary for a company with 10 employees or less: it can answer N/A.

ECO-CIRCULAIRE-DESC.name: How circular economy principles are applied
ECO-CIRCULAIRE-DESC.definition: Describe how the company applies these principles.

DEC-RECYCLES.name: Waste diverted to recycling
DEC-RECYCLES.definition: Waste of the site sent to recycling, excluding energy recovery and backfilling. Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Service provider reports.

DEC-REEMPLOI.name: Waste diverted to preparation for reuse
DEC-REEMPLOI.definition: Waste of the site prepared for reuse (checking, cleaning, repair). Enter 0 if there is none (N/A would make the total not applicable). Source: Service provider reports.

DEC-PAR-CODE.name: Waste by code
DEC-PAR-CODE.unit: table: Waste code, Waste generated, Of which sent to recycling, Of which prepared for reuse
DEC-PAR-CODE.definition: Optional, in addition to the totals: one row per waste code of the European list, with the mass generated and what was sent to recycling or prepared for reuse, in tonnes. Source: Waste register, waste transfer notes.

ECO-MATIERES.name: Material flows used
ECO-MATIERES.definition: For a sector with significant material flows (manufacturing, construction, packaging): one row per key material, with the quantity used over the year and its unit. Voluntary for a company with 10 employees or less: it can answer N/A. Source: Purchasing, bills of materials.

SOC-EFF-HOMMES.name: Male headcount at end of period
SOC-EFF-HOMMES.definition: Men on the payroll at the end of the period. Source: HR information system.

SOC-EFF-GENRE-AUTRE.name: Headcount of other gender at end of period
SOC-EFF-GENRE-AUTRE.definition: Employees who declared another gender, at the end of the period. Source: HR information system.

SOC-EFF-GENRE-NC.name: Headcount with gender not reported at end of period
SOC-EFF-GENRE-NC.definition: Employees whose gender is not reported, at the end of the period. Source: HR information system.

SOC-ACCIDENTS-ENREG.name: Recordable work-related accidents
SOC-ACCIDENTS-ENREG.definition: Work-related accidents of employees during the period that resulted in death or more than 3 days of absence. Accidents of non-employees (agency workers, self-employed people) are not counted here. Source: Accident register, accident reports.

SOC-SALAIRE-MINIMUM.name: Pay at or above the minimum wage
SOC-SALAIRE-MINIMUM.definition: Do all employees receive pay at or above the applicable minimum wage (law or collective agreement)?

SOC-ECART-OBLIGATION.name: Pay gap already reported by obligation
SOC-ECART-OBLIGATION.definition: Is the company already required to report the gender pay gap (EU or national law)? If yes, it gives the hourly pay below (EFRAG's workbook calculates the gap); if not, it answers N/A to both.

SOC-REMU-H-HOMMES.name: Average gross hourly pay of male employees
SOC-REMU-H-HOMMES.definition: Annual gross pay of men (all pay elements included) divided by their hours worked. Method of the Voluntary Standard VS: the gap is calculated in EFRAG's workbook from the two hourly pay figures (B10 §42(b)); ESRS S1 and pay transparency have their own KPIs and their own calculation. Restricted data. Source: Payroll.

SOC-REMU-H-FEMMES.name: Average gross hourly pay of female employees
SOC-REMU-H-FEMMES.definition: Annual gross pay of women (all pay elements included) divided by their hours worked. Method of the Voluntary Standard VS: the gap is calculated in EFRAG's workbook from the two hourly pay figures (B10 §42(b)); ESRS S1 and pay transparency have their own KPIs and their own calculation. Restricted data. Source: Payroll.

SOC-SAL-CONVENTION.name: Employees covered by collective bargaining agreements
SOC-SAL-CONVENTION.definition: Employees covered by a collective agreement, at the end of the period (headcount). Source: HR information system.

STR-PRODUITS.name: Significant groups of products and services
STR-PRODUITS.definition: Describe the significant groups of products and services offered. Voluntary for a company with 10 employees or less: it can answer N/A.

STR-MARCHES.name: Significant markets
STR-MARCHES.definition: Describe the significant markets (for example business-to-business, wholesale, retail, countries). Voluntary for a company with 10 employees or less: it can answer N/A.

STR-RELATIONS.name: Main business relationships
STR-RELATIONS.definition: Describe the main business relationships (key suppliers and their estimated number, sectors and countries, customers, distribution channels). Voluntary for a company with 10 employees or less: it can answer N/A.

STR-ENJEUX.name: Strategy elements related to sustainability
STR-ENJEUX.definition: Does the strategy have key elements related to sustainability issues? Voluntary for a company with 10 employees or less: it can answer N/A.

STR-ENJEUX-DESC.name: Description of the strategy elements related to sustainability
STR-ENJEUX-DESC.definition: Describe these key elements of the strategy.

GOV-C2-DESC.name: Description of practices, policies and initiatives
GOV-C2-DESC.definition: Short description of the practices, policies and initiatives reported in B2; say whether they also cover suppliers or customers.

GOV-C2-CIBLES.name: Description of the targets related to policies
GOV-C2-CIBLES.definition: Describe the targets set for these policies.

GOV-C2-RESPONSABLE.name: Most senior level accountable for practices and policies
GOV-C2-RESPONSABLE.definition: Most senior person or body accountable for implementation (optional).

GES-CIBLES.name: Greenhouse gas reduction targets
GES-CIBLES.definition: Has the company set reduction targets for its emissions (scopes 1 and 2, and 3 if any)? Voluntary for a company with 10 employees or less: it can answer N/A.

GES-ANNEE-REF.name: Base year of the targets
GES-ANNEE-REF.definition: Base year of the reduction targets. Source: Climate strategy or transition plan, base-year emissions inventory.

GES-ANNEE-CIBLE.name: Target year
GES-ANNEE-CIBLE.definition: Year by which the targets must be met. Source: Climate strategy or transition plan, base-year emissions inventory.

GES-S1-REF.name: Scope 1 in the base year
GES-S1-REF.definition: Scope 1 emissions in the base year. Source: Climate strategy or transition plan, base-year emissions inventory.

GES-S1-CIBLE.name: Scope 1 target
GES-S1-CIBLE.definition: Scope 1 emissions targeted for the target year. Source: Climate strategy or transition plan, base-year emissions inventory.

GES-S2-LB-REF.name: Scope 2 (location-based) in the base year
GES-S2-LB-REF.definition: Location-based scope 2 emissions in the base year. Source: Climate strategy or transition plan, base-year emissions inventory.

GES-S2-LB-CIBLE.name: Scope 2 (location-based) target
GES-S2-LB-CIBLE.definition: Location-based scope 2 emissions targeted for the target year. Source: Climate strategy or transition plan, base-year emissions inventory.

GES-S2-MB-REF.name: Scope 2 (market-based) in the base year
GES-S2-MB-REF.definition: Market-based scope 2 emissions in the base year (optional). Source: Climate strategy or transition plan, base-year emissions inventory.

GES-S2-MB-CIBLE.name: Scope 2 (market-based) target
GES-S2-MB-CIBLE.definition: Market-based scope 2 emissions targeted for the target year (optional). Source: Climate strategy or transition plan, base-year emissions inventory.

GES-S3-CIBLES.name: Scope 3 targets by category
GES-S3-CIBLES.unit: table: Category, Base-year emissions, Target-year emissions
GES-S3-CIBLES.definition: If the company has set scope 3 targets: one row per category, with the base-year emissions and those targeted for the target year. Source: Climate strategy or transition plan, base-year emissions inventory.

GES-ACTIONS.name: Main actions to achieve the targets
GES-ACTIONS.definition: List the main actions planned to achieve the targets.

GES-PLAN-STATUT.name: Status of the transition plan
GES-PLAN-STATUT.unit: list: Adoption of a transition plan is planned in the future, A transition plan has already been adopted, A transition plan is not in place and it is not planned to be adopted
GES-PLAN-STATUT.definition: Is a transition plan for climate change mitigation adopted, planned, or neither? The planned year of adoption is entered separately. Who answers: in the Voluntary Standard VS, a company in a high climate impact sector (C3 §54-55); in the ESRS, every company, an adopted plan being one that includes the key features of E1-1 §12(a) (E1-1 §13).

GES-PLAN-DESC.name: Description of the transition plan
GES-PLAN-DESC.definition: Describe the transition plan and how it reduces emissions (optional).

GES-PLAN-ANNEE.name: Planned year of adoption of the transition plan
GES-PLAN-ANNEE.definition: If the plan is not adopted yet: year planned for its adoption. Source: Climate strategy or transition plan, base-year emissions inventory.

GES-PLAN-MOIS.name: Planned month of adoption of the transition plan
GES-PLAN-MOIS.definition: Month (1 to 12), with the year above. Source: Climate strategy or transition plan, base-year emissions inventory.

GES-PLAN-JOUR.name: Planned day of adoption of the transition plan
GES-PLAN-JOUR.definition: Day (1 to 31), with the month and year above. Source: Climate strategy or transition plan, base-year emissions inventory.

CLI-RISQUES.name: Climate hazards and transition events identified
CLI-RISQUES.definition: Has the company identified climate-related hazards and transition events? Voluntary for a company with 10 employees or less: it can answer N/A.

CLI-ALEAS.name: Climate hazards and transition events
CLI-ALEAS.definition: Describe the climate-related hazards and transition events.

CLI-EXPOSITION.name: Assessment of exposure and sensitivity
CLI-EXPOSITION.definition: How the company assessed the exposure and sensitivity of its assets, activities and value chain.

CLI-HORIZONS.name: Time horizons of the hazards and events
CLI-HORIZONS.definition: Short term: 1 year; medium term: 2 to 5 years; long term: more than 5 years.

CLI-ADAPTATION.name: Climate change adaptation actions
CLI-ADAPTATION.definition: Has the company taken adaptation actions for these hazards and events?

CLI-EFFETS.name: Potential financial effects of climate risks
CLI-EFFETS.definition: Potential adverse effects on financial performance or operations, in the short, medium or long term (optional).

SOC-DEPARTS-CDI.name: Leavers on permanent contracts
SOC-DEPARTS-CDI.definition: Employees on permanent contracts who left during the period (resignation, dismissal, retirement, death in service), as a headcount. Source: HR information system.

SOC-EFFECTIF-DEBUT.name: Headcount at the start of the period
SOC-EFFECTIF-DEBUT.definition: Only for the first year tracked in the tool: employees on the payroll at the start of the period. In the following years, the headcount at the end of the previous year is the starting point of the turnover rate. Source: HR information system.

SOC-MANAGERS-FEMMES.name: Women at management level
SOC-MANAGERS-FEMMES.definition: Women at management level, at period end (optional). Source: HR information system.

SOC-MANAGERS-HOMMES.name: Men at management level
SOC-MANAGERS-HOMMES.definition: Men at management level, at period end (optional). Source: HR information system.

SOC-INDEPENDANTS.name: Self-employed working exclusively for the company
SOC-INDEPENDANTS.definition: Self-employed workers without employees working exclusively for the company (optional). Source: Purchasing, service contracts.

SOC-INTERIMAIRES.name: Temporary agency workers
SOC-INTERIMAIRES.definition: Temporary workers provided by employment agencies (optional). Source: Temporary agency invoices.

SOC-CODE-CONDUITE.name: Code of conduct or human rights policy
SOC-CODE-CONDUITE.definition: Does the company have a code of conduct or human rights policy for its own workforce? Voluntary for a company with 10 employees or less: it can answer N/A.

SOC-CODE-ENFANTS.name: Code of conduct: child labour
SOC-CODE-ENFANTS.definition: Does the code of conduct or policy cover: child labour?

SOC-CODE-FORCE.name: Code of conduct: forced labour
SOC-CODE-FORCE.definition: Does the code of conduct or policy cover: forced labour?

SOC-CODE-TRAITE.name: Code of conduct: human trafficking
SOC-CODE-TRAITE.definition: Does the code of conduct or policy cover: human trafficking?

SOC-CODE-DISCRIMINATION.name: Code of conduct: discrimination
SOC-CODE-DISCRIMINATION.definition: Does the code of conduct or policy cover: discrimination?

SOC-CODE-ACCIDENTS.name: Code of conduct: accident prevention
SOC-CODE-ACCIDENTS.definition: Does the code of conduct or policy cover: accident prevention?

SOC-CODE-AUTRE.name: Code of conduct: other topic
SOC-CODE-AUTRE.definition: Does the code of conduct or policy cover: other topic?

SOC-CODE-AUTRE-DESC.name: Other topics covered by the code of conduct

SOC-PLAINTES.name: Complaints-handling mechanism for the workforce
SOC-PLAINTES.definition: Does the company have a complaints-handling mechanism for its own workforce?

SOC-INCIDENTS.name: Confirmed incidents in the own workforce
SOC-INCIDENTS.definition: Were there confirmed incidents (established by a court, the OECD or an authority) in the own workforce? Voluntary for a company with 10 employees or less: it can answer N/A.

SOC-INCIDENT-ENFANTS.name: Confirmed incident: child labour
SOC-INCIDENT-ENFANTS.definition: Does a confirmed incident relate to: child labour?

SOC-INCIDENT-FORCE.name: Confirmed incident: forced labour
SOC-INCIDENT-FORCE.definition: Does a confirmed incident relate to: forced labour?

SOC-INCIDENT-TRAITE.name: Confirmed incident: human trafficking
SOC-INCIDENT-TRAITE.definition: Does a confirmed incident relate to: human trafficking?

SOC-INCIDENT-DISCRIMINATION.name: Confirmed incident: discrimination
SOC-INCIDENT-DISCRIMINATION.definition: Does a confirmed incident relate to: discrimination?

SOC-INCIDENT-AUTRE.name: Confirmed incident: other human right
SOC-INCIDENT-AUTRE.definition: Does a confirmed incident relate to: other human right?

SOC-INCIDENT-AUTRE-DESC.name: Other human rights concerned by the incidents
SOC-INCIDENT-AUTRE-DESC.definition: Specify the other human rights concerned.

SOC-INCIDENTS-ACTIONS.name: Actions taken after the confirmed incidents

SOC-INCIDENTS-CHAINE.name: Confirmed incidents in the value chain
SOC-INCIDENTS-CHAINE.definition: Is the company aware of confirmed incidents during the period involving value chain workers, affected communities, consumers or end-users? Voluntary for a company with 10 employees or less: it can answer N/A.

SOC-INCIDENTS-CHAINE-DESC.name: Description of the incidents in the value chain

GOV-REV-SECTEURS.name: Revenues from certain activities
GOV-REV-SECTEURS.definition: Does the company derive revenues from one of the activities below (prohibited weapons, tobacco, fossil fuels, chemicals)?

GOV-REV-ARMES.name: Revenue from prohibited weapons
GOV-REV-ARMES.definition: Anti-personnel mines, cluster munitions, chemical and biological weapons. Source: Accounting.

GOV-REV-TABAC.name: Revenue from tobacco
GOV-REV-TABAC.definition: Cultivation and production of tobacco. Source: Accounting.

GOV-REV-CHIMIE.name: Revenue from chemicals production
GOV-REV-CHIMIE.definition: Manufacture of pesticides and other agrochemical products (NACE group 20.2). Source: Accounting.

GOV-ORGANE.name: Governance body in place
GOV-ORGANE.definition: Does the company have a governance body (board of directors, supervisory board)?

GOV-CA-FEMMES.name: Female members of the governance body
GOV-CA-FEMMES.definition: Female members of the governance body at period end. Source: Articles of association, minutes, register of directors.

GOV-CA-HOMMES.name: Male members of the governance body
GOV-CA-HOMMES.definition: Male members of the governance body at period end. Source: Articles of association, minutes, register of directors.

SOC-ECART-DECL-SOUMIS.name: Employer required to report this year
SOC-ECART-DECL-SOUMIS.definition: Yes if the employer must report its pay gaps for this year. Thresholds of the directive: 250 workers or more, every year (first report in 2027 on the year 2026); 150 to 249, every three years (first report in 2027); 100 to 149, every three years (first report in 2031). Fewer than 100: voluntary, unless national law requires it. National law sets the exact dates.

SOC-REMU-NB-F.name: Women included in the pay gap calculation
SOC-REMU-NB-F.definition: Number of female workers of the employer included in the calculation of average pay: all contracts, including part-time and fixed-term workers, and agency workers when national law assigns them to the employer. An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-REMU-NB-H.name: Men included in the pay gap calculation
SOC-REMU-NB-H.definition: Number of male workers of the employer included in the calculation of average pay, on the same perimeter as women. An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-REMU-MOY-AN-F.name: Average gross annual pay of women
SOC-REMU-MOY-AN-F.definition: Average gross annual pay of the women included: basic wage or salary and all other components, in cash or in kind (bonuses, variable pay, benefits). Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-REMU-MOY-AN-H.name: Average gross annual pay of men
SOC-REMU-MOY-AN-H.definition: Average gross annual pay of the men included, with the same components as for women. Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-REMU-MOY-HOR-F.name: Average gross hourly pay of women
SOC-REMU-MOY-HOR-F.definition: Average gross hourly pay of the women included (the annual pay of each one divided by her paid hours). Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-REMU-MOY-HOR-H.name: Average gross hourly pay of men
SOC-REMU-MOY-HOR-H.definition: Average gross hourly pay of the men included (the annual pay of each one divided by his paid hours). Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-REMU-VAR-NB-F.name: Women who receive variable pay
SOC-REMU-VAR-NB-F.definition: Number of the women included who received a complementary or variable component during the year (bonuses, commissions, profit-sharing…). Enter 0 if there is none. An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-REMU-VAR-NB-H.name: Men who receive variable pay
SOC-REMU-VAR-NB-H.definition: Number of the men included who received a complementary or variable component during the year. Enter 0 if there is none. An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-REMU-VAR-MOY-F.name: Average annual variable pay of women who receive it
SOC-REMU-VAR-MOY-F.definition: Average gross complementary or variable components of the year, over the women who received one only. N/A if no woman received one. Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-REMU-VAR-MOY-H.name: Average annual variable pay of men who receive it
SOC-REMU-VAR-MOY-H.definition: Average gross complementary or variable components of the year, over the men who received one only. N/A if no man received one. Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-REMU-TOT-AN-F.name: Total annual pay of women
SOC-REMU-TOT-AN-F.definition: Calculation data, calculated by the tool: it adds up from one entity to the next, so that the group gap is recalculated from the totals.

SOC-REMU-TOT-AN-H.name: Total annual pay of men
SOC-REMU-TOT-AN-H.definition: Calculation data, calculated by the tool: it adds up from one entity to the next, so that the group gap is recalculated from the totals.

SOC-REMU-TOT-HOR-F.name: Sum of the hourly pay of women
SOC-REMU-TOT-HOR-F.definition: Calculation data, calculated by the tool: it adds up from one entity to the next, so that the group gap is recalculated from the totals.

SOC-REMU-TOT-HOR-H.name: Sum of the hourly pay of men
SOC-REMU-TOT-HOR-H.definition: Calculation data, calculated by the tool: it adds up from one entity to the next, so that the group gap is recalculated from the totals.

SOC-REMU-VAR-TOT-F.name: Total variable pay of women
SOC-REMU-VAR-TOT-F.definition: Calculation data, calculated by the tool: it adds up from one entity to the next, so that the group gap is recalculated from the totals.

SOC-REMU-VAR-TOT-H.name: Total variable pay of men
SOC-REMU-VAR-TOT-H.definition: Calculation data, calculated by the tool: it adds up from one entity to the next, so that the group gap is recalculated from the totals.

SOC-ECART-MOY-HOR.name: Gender pay gap (hourly)
SOC-ECART-MOY-HOR.definition: Calculated by the tool: difference between the average hourly pay of men and that of women, as a share of men's. Positive when women are paid less. Recalculated at each level from the totals: the group gap is not the average of the entities' gaps. Method of Directive (EU) 2023/970, per employer; the Voluntary Standard VS and ESRS S1 have their own KPIs and their own calculation.

SOC-ECART-MOY-AN.name: Gender pay gap (annual)
SOC-ECART-MOY-AN.definition: Calculated by the tool, like the hourly gap, from the average annual pay.

SOC-ECART-MED-HOR.name: Median gender pay gap (hourly)
SOC-ECART-MED-HOR.definition: Difference between the median hourly pay of men and that of women, as a share of men's (the median splits the workers into two halves: one earns more, the other less). Entered by the entity: the median of a group cannot be derived from those of its entities. Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-ECART-MED-AN.name: Median gender pay gap (annual)
SOC-ECART-MED-AN.definition: Like the hourly median gap, from the annual pay. Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-ECART-VAR-MOY.name: Gender pay gap in variable pay
SOC-ECART-VAR-MOY.definition: Calculated by the tool: difference between the average variable pay of the men and of the women who receive it, as a share of men's. Recalculated at each level from the totals.

SOC-ECART-VAR-MED.name: Median gender pay gap in variable pay
SOC-ECART-VAR-MED.definition: Difference between the median variable pay of the men and of the women who receive it, as a share of men's. Entered by the entity. Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-REMU-VAR-PART-F.name: Share of women who receive variable pay
SOC-REMU-VAR-PART-F.definition: Calculated by the tool, at each level.

SOC-REMU-VAR-PART-H.name: Share of men who receive variable pay
SOC-REMU-VAR-PART-H.definition: Calculated by the tool, at each level.

SOC-QUARTILE-1-F.name: Share of women in pay quartile 1 (lowest)
SOC-QUARTILE-1-F.definition: Rank the workers from the lowest to the highest pay level and cut the list into four groups of the same size. Share of women in group 1 (lowest). Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-QUARTILE-1-H.name: Share of men in pay quartile 1 (lowest)
SOC-QUARTILE-1-H.definition: Calculated by the tool: 100% minus the share of women in the same quartile. No value above the entity: the quartiles of a group cannot be derived from those of its entities.

SOC-QUARTILE-2-F.name: Share of women in pay quartile 2 (lower middle)
SOC-QUARTILE-2-F.definition: Rank the workers from the lowest to the highest pay level and cut the list into four groups of the same size. Share of women in group 2 (lower middle). Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-QUARTILE-2-H.name: Share of men in pay quartile 2 (lower middle)
SOC-QUARTILE-2-H.definition: Calculated by the tool: 100% minus the share of women in the same quartile. No value above the entity: the quartiles of a group cannot be derived from those of its entities.

SOC-QUARTILE-3-F.name: Share of women in pay quartile 3 (upper middle)
SOC-QUARTILE-3-F.definition: Rank the workers from the lowest to the highest pay level and cut the list into four groups of the same size. Share of women in group 3 (upper middle). Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-QUARTILE-3-H.name: Share of men in pay quartile 3 (upper middle)
SOC-QUARTILE-3-H.definition: Calculated by the tool: 100% minus the share of women in the same quartile. No value above the entity: the quartiles of a group cannot be derived from those of its entities.

SOC-QUARTILE-4-F.name: Share of women in pay quartile 4 (highest)
SOC-QUARTILE-4-F.definition: Rank the workers from the lowest to the highest pay level and cut the list into four groups of the same size. Share of women in group 4 (highest). Calculation method: the one set by national law (for example for part-time workers). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll.

SOC-QUARTILE-4-H.name: Share of men in pay quartile 4 (highest)
SOC-QUARTILE-4-H.definition: Calculated by the tool: 100% minus the share of women in the same quartile. No value above the entity: the quartiles of a group cannot be derived from those of its entities.

SOC-ECART-CATEGORIES.name: Gender pay gap by category of workers
SOC-ECART-CATEGORIES.unit: table: Category of workers, Women, Men, Gap in basic wage or salary (%), Gap in variable components (%)
SOC-ECART-CATEGORIES.definition: One row per category of workers (people who do the same work or work of equal value, grouped by the employer on neutral criteria: skills, effort, responsibility, working conditions). For each category: number of women and men, gap in basic wage or salary and gap in variable components, as a % of the average pay of men. An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong). Source: Payroll and job classification.

SOC-ECART-CAT-5PCT.name: Gap of at least 5% in a category
SOC-ECART-CAT-5PCT.definition: Yes if the average pay gap between women and men is 5% or more in at least one category of workers. An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong).

SOC-EVAL-CONJOINTE-REQUISE.name: Joint pay assessment required
SOC-EVAL-CONJOINTE-REQUISE.definition: Yes if a gap of at least 5% in a category is neither justified by objective, gender-neutral criteria nor remedied within six months of the report: the employer must then carry out a joint pay assessment with the workers' representatives. An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong).

SOC-EVAL-CONJOINTE-MENEE.name: Joint pay assessment carried out and shared
SOC-EVAL-CONJOINTE-MENEE.definition: Yes if the joint pay assessment was carried out with the workers' representatives, then made available to the workers and sent to the monitoring body. N/A if it is not required. An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong).

SOC-ECART-CONFIRME.name: Accuracy confirmed by management
SOC-ECART-CONFIRME.definition: Yes if management confirmed the accuracy of the information, after consulting the workers' representatives (who have access to the calculation method). An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong).

SOC-ECART-TRANSMIS.name: Information sent to the authority
SOC-ECART-TRANSMIS.definition: Yes if all the information of the report (gaps, variable pay, quartiles, categories) was sent to the national authority in charge of collecting it. An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong).

SOC-ECART-CAT-DIFFUSE.name: Gaps by category shared with the workers
SOC-ECART-CAT-DIFFUSE.definition: Yes if the gaps by category of workers were shared with all the workers and their representatives. An employer that does not report this year answers N/A, here and for all the other pay data (otherwise the group total would be wrong).

SOC-ECART-PUBLIE.name: Gaps published by the employer
SOC-ECART-PUBLIE.definition: Optional. Yes if the employer also publishes its gaps (except those by category), for example on its website.

SOC-REMU-INFO-CANDIDATS.name: Starting pay given to applicants
SOC-REMU-INFO-CANDIDATS.definition: Yes if applicants receive, before the interview (for example in the job vacancy notice), the starting pay of the position or its range, and the rules of the collective agreement that apply to it.

SOC-REMU-HISTO-NON-DEMANDE.name: No question on pay history
SOC-REMU-HISTO-NON-DEMANDE.definition: Yes if recruiters never ask applicants about their current or previous pay.

SOC-REMU-CRITERES-ACCES.name: Pay criteria accessible to the workers
SOC-REMU-CRITERES-ACCES.definition: Yes if the workers have easy access to the objective, gender-neutral criteria that set their pay, their pay level and its progression. A Member State can exempt employers with fewer than 50 workers from the part on progression.

SOC-REMU-INFO-DROIT.name: Workers informed of their right to information
SOC-REMU-INFO-DROIT.definition: Yes if, this year, all the workers were informed of their right to know their pay level and the average pay levels, by sex, of their category, and of how to ask for it (written answer within two months).

GEN-PERIMETRE-ECART.name: Difference from the boundary of the consolidated financial statements: description and reasons
GEN-PERIMETRE-ECART.definition: Only if the boundary of the own operations used in the sustainability statement differs from the one of the consolidated financial statements: describe the difference and its reasons, for example a subsidiary left out of consolidation because it is not financially material (ESRS 2 §4(a), AR 1). Answer N/A otherwise.

GEN-CHAINE-VALEUR.name: Coverage of the upstream and downstream value chain
GEN-CHAINE-VALEUR.definition: Overview of the extent to which the sustainability statement covers the company's upstream and downstream value chain (ESRS 2 §4(b)).

GEN-CONFORMITE-ESRS.name: Compliance with the ESRS and version applied
GEN-CONFORMITE-ESRS.unit: list: Revised ESRS (Delegated Regulation 2026/1563), First set of ESRS (Delegated Regulation 2023/2772), First set of ESRS with the reliefs of Article 2(1)(b) of Delegated Regulation 2026/1563, Not fully compliant / voluntary use of the ESRS
GEN-CONFORMITE-ESRS.definition: Statement that the sustainability statement is prepared in accordance with the ESRS applicable at the end of the reporting period, and set of standards applied (ESRS 2 §5). For a financial year starting in 2026, Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1563 allows the first set of ESRS, the revised ESRS, or the first set with certain reliefs of the revised ESRS, and asks to state the version applied (Article 2); the revised ESRS apply to financial years starting on or after 1 January 2027 (Article 3).

GEN-DISPOSITIONS.name: Reliefs, options and specific provisions of ESRS 1 applied
GEN-DISPOSITIONS.definition: List of the reliefs, options or specific provisions of ESRS 1 that the company applies (ESRS 2 §6). Cases to consider (AR 2): acquisitions and disposals; other time horizons; changes in preparation or presentation; adjusted comparative information; material judgement and significant uncertainty; omission of information; activities excluded from the calculation of a metric; partial boundary of a metric for lack of reliable data; joint operations excluded from environmental metrics; limitations due to undue cost or effort; events after the end of the period; prior-period errors. Answer N/A if none is applied.

GEN-DISPOSITIONS-INFOS.name: Information required by the reliefs and provisions applied
GEN-DISPOSITIONS-INFOS.definition: For each relief, option or specific provision applied, the information that ESRS 1 requires with it (ESRS 2 §6). It can also be given next to the disclosure concerned (AR 2): then say where. Answer N/A if none is applied.

GEN-LIENS-ETATS-FIN.name: Connectivity with the financial statements and differences in assumptions
GEN-LIENS-ETATS-FIN.definition: For the amounts also presented in the financial statements: the cross-reference to the financial statements (ESRS 1 §114); for the amounts that are an aggregation or part of them: how they relate to the most relevant amounts of the financial statements (ESRS 1 §115); and any significant differences between the assumptions of the sustainability statement and those of the financial statements (ESRS 1 §116). Answer N/A if there are none. Source: Accounting, financial statements.

GEN-PROGRESSIF-IRO.name: Phase-in: materiality of the topics omitted
GEN-PROGRESSIF-IRO.definition: Only if the company omits all disclosures of one or more topical standards under the phase-in provisions of ESRS 1 (§125(a), §126(a) or §127(a)); answer N/A otherwise. For each topic omitted, say whether its impacts, risks and opportunities were assessed as material by the materiality assessment, and which ones (ESRS 2 §8).

GEN-PROGRESSIF-SUJETS.name: Phase-in: material topics omitted
GEN-PROGRESSIF-SUJETS.definition: Only if the company omits all disclosures of one or more topical standards under the phase-in provisions of ESRS 1 (§125(a), §126(a) or §127(a)); answer N/A otherwise. Topics or sub-topics assessed as material whose disclosures are omitted (ESRS 2 §9(a)).

GEN-PROGRESSIF-STRATEGIE.name: Phase-in: impacts of the topics omitted in the strategy
GEN-PROGRESSIF-STRATEGIE.definition: Only if the company omits all disclosures of one or more topical standards under the phase-in provisions of ESRS 1 (§125(a), §126(a) or §127(a)); answer N/A otherwise. For each material topic or sub-topic omitted, short description of how the business model and the strategy take account of its impacts (ESRS 2 §9(a)).

GEN-PROGRESSIF-CIBLES.name: Phase-in: time-bound targets and progress on the topics omitted
GEN-PROGRESSIF-CIBLES.definition: Only if the company omits all disclosures of one or more topical standards under the phase-in provisions of ESRS 1 (§125(a), §126(a) or §127(a)); answer N/A otherwise. Short description of the time-bound targets set on these topics and of the progress made towards them (ESRS 2 §9(b)).

GEN-PROGRESSIF-BIO-SCIENCE.name: Phase-in: science-based biodiversity targets
GEN-PROGRESSIF-BIO-SCIENCE.definition: Only if the company omits all disclosures of one or more topical standards under the phase-in provisions of ESRS 1 (§125(a), §126(a) or §127(a)); answer N/A otherwise. Are the targets on biodiversity and ecosystems based on conclusive scientific evidence (ESRS 2 §9(b))? Answer N/A if biodiversity is not a material topic omitted or has no target.

GEN-PROGRESSIF-POLITIQUES.name: Phase-in: policies on the topics omitted
GEN-PROGRESSIF-POLITIQUES.definition: Only if the company omits all disclosures of one or more topical standards under the phase-in provisions of ESRS 1 (§125(a), §126(a) or §127(a)); answer N/A otherwise. Short description of the policies on these topics (ESRS 2 §9(c)).

GEN-PROGRESSIF-ACTIONS.name: Phase-in: actions on the topics omitted and their results
GEN-PROGRESSIF-ACTIONS.definition: Only if the company omits all disclosures of one or more topical standards under the phase-in provisions of ESRS 1 (§125(a), §126(a) or §127(a)); answer N/A otherwise. Short description of the actions taken to identify, monitor, prevent, mitigate, bring to an end, minimise or remediate the actual or potential negative impacts of these topics, and of their results (ESRS 2 §9(d)).

GEN-PROGRESSIF-INDICATEURS.name: Phase-in: metrics on the topics omitted
GEN-PROGRESSIF-INDICATEURS.definition: Only if the company omits all disclosures of one or more topical standards under the phase-in provisions of ESRS 1 (§125(a), §126(a) or §127(a)); answer N/A otherwise. Metrics relevant to these topics, with their values (ESRS 2 §9(e)).

GEN-PROGRESSIF-OMIS.name: Other information omitted under the phase-in provisions
GEN-PROGRESSIF-OMIS.definition: Does the company omit information under the other phase-in provisions of ESRS 1 (§125(b)-(e), §126(b)-(e), §127(b)-(e): anticipated financial effects, substances of concern and of very high concern)? The standard asks to say so (ESRS 2 §10). If yes, say which in the general part of the statement or in the content index (AR 4). Paragraph 10 covers points (b) to (e) only; the reliefs specific to ESRS S1 (§125(f), §126(f), §127(f): S1-6, S1-7 outside the EEA, S1-10 to S1-12, S1-13 §37(d)-(e) and non-employees, S1-14) are reported in the same way if they are used.

GOV-CA-INDEPENDANTS.name: Independent members of the governance body
GOV-CA-INDEPENDANTS.definition: Independent members of the board (administrative or supervisory body) at period end, counted among all the members of the body (ESRS 2 §12(a)). Source: Minutes and terms of reference of the administrative, management or supervisory body, corporate governance report.

GOV-CA-AUTRES.name: Members of the governance body of another gender or whose gender is not reported
GOV-CA-AUTRES.definition: Members of the board (administrative or supervisory body) at period end who are counted neither among the women nor among the men: another gender, or gender not reported (ESRS 2 §12(a)). Enter 0 if there is none; N/A also counts as 0 in the number of members. Source: Minutes and terms of reference of the administrative, management or supervisory body, corporate governance report.

GOV-CA-MEMBRES.name: Members of the governance body, all genders
GOV-CA-MEMBRES.definition: Calculated by the tool: women, men, and members of another gender or whose gender is not reported, at period end; an N/A number of other members counts as 0. Denominator of the shares of §12(a) (ESRS 2 §12(a)).

GOV-CA-PART-INDEP.name: Share of independent members of the governance body
GOV-CA-PART-INDEP.definition: Calculated by the tool: independent members divided by all the members of the body (women, men, another gender or gender not reported) at period end (ESRS 2 §12(a)).

GOV-CA-RATIO-FH.name: hommes) / Gender diversity of the governance body (ratio of women to men)
GOV-CA-RATIO-FH.definition: Calculated by the tool: number of female members divided by the number of male members of the body at period end, as AR 6 requires (ESRS 2 §12(a)). 50% = one woman for two men. This ratio counts women and men only; members of another gender or whose gender is not reported are not in it.

GOV-CA-PART-FEMMES.name: Share of women on the governance body
GOV-CA-PART-FEMMES.definition: Calculated by the tool: women members of the body divided by all the members of the body (women, men, another gender or gender not reported) at period end, the percentage by gender of §12(a) (ESRS 2 §12(a)). The ratio of women to men of AR 6, which counts women and men only, is calculated separately.

GOV-CA-PART-HOMMES.name: Share of men on the governance body
GOV-CA-PART-HOMMES.definition: Calculated by the tool: men members of the body divided by all the members of the body (women, men, another gender or gender not reported) at period end, the percentage by gender of §12(a) (ESRS 2 §12(a)). The ratio of women to men of AR 6, which counts women and men only, is calculated separately.

GOV-CA-PART-AUTRES.name: Share of members of another gender or whose gender is not reported on the governance body
GOV-CA-PART-AUTRES.definition: Calculated by the tool: members of another gender or whose gender is not reported divided by all the members of the body (women, men, another gender or gender not reported) at period end, the percentage by gender of §12(a) (ESRS 2 §12(a)). The ratio of women to men of AR 6, which counts women and men only, is calculated separately.

GOV-CA-REPRESENTATION.name: Representation of employees and other workers in the bodies
GOV-CA-REPRESENTATION.definition: If employees and other workers are represented in the administrative, management or supervisory bodies: how (number of seats, how they are appointed) (ESRS 2 §12(a)). Answer N/A otherwise.

GOV-CA-DIVERSITE.name: Other aspects of diversity of the bodies
GOV-CA-DIVERSITE.definition: Breakdown of the members of the bodies by the other aspects of diversity that the company takes into account (age, nationality, background…), as percentages (ESRS 2 §12(a)).

GOV-CA-COMPETENCES.name: Sustainability expertise and skills of the bodies
GOV-CA-COMPETENCES.definition: Expertise and skills of the bodies, held directly or accessible to them, to oversee and manage the material impacts, risks and opportunities, and how they make sure these skills are available or will be developed (ESRS 2 §12(b), AR 7).

GOV-CA-RESPONSABILITES.name: Persons or committees responsible for impacts, risks and opportunities
GOV-CA-RESPONSABILITES.definition: Identity and responsibilities of the persons, committees or bodies within the governance bodies in charge of managing or overseeing the material impacts, risks and opportunities, as set out in mandates and terms of reference; indicate those that the bodies address themselves without delegating key decisions (ESRS 2 §12(c), AR 8).

GOV-CA-SUIVI-CIBLES.name: Targets: setting and monitoring by the bodies
GOV-CA-SUIVI-CIBLES.definition: How the bodies manage or oversee the setting of targets related to the material impacts, risks and opportunities, and how they monitor progress towards them (ESRS 2 §12(d)).

GOV-CA-PRISE-EN-COMPTE.name: How the bodies take impacts, risks and opportunities into account
GOV-CA-PRISE-EN-COMPTE.definition: How the bodies take the material impacts, risks and opportunities into account in the strategy, the decisions on major transactions and risk management, and how they weigh trade-offs between them if they do (ESRS 2 §12(e)).

GOV-CA-ARBITRAGES.name: Trade-offs considered by the bodies
GOV-CA-ARBITRAGES.definition: Have the bodies or the persons concerned considered the trade-offs associated with the material impacts, risks and opportunities (ESRS 2 §12(e))?

GOV-REMU-LIEN.name: Incentive schemes linked to sustainability
GOV-REMU-LIEN.definition: Do the members of the administrative, management or supervisory bodies have incentive schemes linked to sustainability topics? The four disclosures that follow are required only if yes (ESRS 2 §14).

GOV-REMU-DURABILITE.name: Link between the remuneration of the bodies and sustainability
GOV-REMU-DURABILITE.definition: How the remuneration of the members of the bodies is linked to sustainability topics (ESRS 2 §14). Answer N/A without such an incentive scheme.

GOV-REMU-DISPOSITIFS.name: Incentive schemes: key characteristics
GOV-REMU-DISPOSITIFS.definition: Description of the key characteristics of the incentive schemes linked to sustainability (ESRS 2 §14(a)). Answer N/A without such a scheme.

GOV-REMU-CRITERES.name: Incentive schemes: sustainability targets or metrics used
GOV-REMU-CRITERES.definition: If performance is assessed against specific sustainability targets or metrics: which ones (ESRS 2 §14(b)). Answer N/A otherwise.

GOV-REMU-PART-VARIABLE.name: Share of variable remuneration linked to sustainability targets
GOV-REMU-PART-VARIABLE.definition: Share of the variable remuneration of the members of the bodies that depends on sustainability targets or metrics (ESRS 2 §14(c)). Entered as a percentage, once for the company: it comes from the contracts and is not summed. Answer N/A without such a scheme. Source: Remuneration policy of the directors, remuneration report.

GOV-DILIGENCE.name: Statement on due diligence
GOV-DILIGENCE.definition: Where the sustainability statement reflects the main aspects and steps of the due diligence applied to sustainability topics (ESRS 2 §16); a table that maps the steps to the disclosures is suitable (AR 9).

GOV-CONTROLE-INTERNE.name: Risk management and internal control over sustainability reporting
GOV-CONTROLE-INTERNE.definition: Scope, main features and components of the risk management and internal control processes and systems over sustainability reporting, considering the completeness and integrity of the data and the accuracy of estimates (ESRS 2 §18, AR 10).

STR-MODELE-AFFAIRES.name: Business model and value chain
STR-MODELE-AFFAIRES.definition: Description of the business model, of the upstream and downstream value chain and of the company's position in it (ESRS 2 §20(a)).

STR-PRODUITS-MARCHES.name: Significant products, services and markets, and their role for sustainability
STR-PRODUITS-MARCHES.definition: Significant groups of products and services, significant markets or customer groups, their contribution to the company's sustainability objectives, and the significant changes of the period (products, services, markets or customers added or removed) (ESRS 2 §20(b)(i)). Significant: more than 10% of revenue, or connected with actual or potential material impacts (AR 13).

STR-PRODUITS-INTERDITS.name: Products and services banned in certain markets
STR-PRODUITS-INTERDITS.definition: Where applicable and significant, products and services banned in certain markets (ESRS 2 §20(b)(ii), AR 13). Answer N/A otherwise.

STR-SECTEURS.name: Significant sectors of activity
STR-SECTEURS.definition: Significant sectors of the company's own operations (ESRS 2 §20(c), AR 11 to 13), in the classification chosen: NACE, operating segments of the financial statements (IFRS 8) or another recognised classification. Significant: more than 10% of revenue, or connected with material impacts.

STR-ACTIVITES-INTERNES.name: Significant activities internal to the group
STR-ACTIVITES-INTERNES.definition: Activities internal to the group, if they are significant or connected (or may be connected) to material impacts, risks and opportunities; for them, only the connection with material impacts makes a sector significant (ESRS 2 §20(c), AR 13). Answer N/A if there is none.

STR-ACTIF-FOSSILE.name: Active in the fossil fuel sector
STR-ACTIF-FOSSILE.definition: Is the company active in the fossil fuel sector (coal, oil, gas): exploration, extraction, production, processing, storage, refining, distribution, transport or trade (ESRS 2 §20(d)(i), AR 14)? If yes, revenue from coal, oil and gas below.

STR-ACTIF-CHIMIE.name: Active in chemicals production
STR-ACTIF-CHIMIE.definition: Do activities of the company fall under Division 20.2 of NACE (pesticides and other agrochemical products) (ESRS 2 §20(d)(ii))? If yes, related revenue below.

STR-ACTIF-ARMES.name: Active in the prohibited weapons industry
STR-ACTIF-ARMES.definition: Is the company active in the prohibited weapons industry (anti-personnel mines, cluster munitions, chemical or biological weapons) (ESRS 2 §20(d)(iii))? If yes, related revenue below.

STR-ACTIF-TABAC.name: Active in the cultivation and production of tobacco
STR-ACTIF-TABAC.definition: Is the company active in the cultivation and production of tobacco (ESRS 2 §20(d)(iv))? If yes, related revenue below.

STR-PARTIES-PRENANTES.name: Stakeholder engagement and key stakeholders
STR-PARTIES-PRENANTES.definition: Summarised description of the stakeholder engagement and of the key stakeholders the company engaged with, by the categories of affected stakeholders of ESRS 1 (AR 23) (ESRS 2 §22(a)).

STR-PP-ATTENTES.name: Interests and views of key stakeholders
STR-PP-ATTENTES.definition: The company's understanding of the interests and views of its key stakeholders in relation to its strategy and business model (ESRS 2 §22(b)).

GOV-CA-INFO-PP.name: How the bodies are informed of stakeholders' views
GOV-CA-INFO-PP.definition: How the administrative, management or supervisory bodies are informed of the views and interests of the key affected stakeholders, workers' representatives included, on the material impacts, risks and opportunities (ESRS 2 §22(c)).

STR-IRO-INTERACTION.name: Material impacts, risks and opportunities and the strategy
STR-IRO-INTERACTION.definition: High-level description: how the material impacts originate from the strategy and business model, what effects the risks and opportunities have on the business model and value chain, and how the company has addressed and plans to address them in its strategy and decisions (ESRS 2 §24, AR 15).

STR-EFFETS-ACTUELS.name: Current financial effects of material risks and opportunities
STR-EFFETS-ACTUELS.definition: Qualitative and quantitative information (amounts or ranges, or volumes) on how the material risks and opportunities have affected the financial position, financial performance and cash flows of the period (ESRS 2 §25, §32, AR 16 to 20). Quantitative information can be left out in the cases of §28: explain it in the text on information not quantified.

STR-EFFETS-AJUSTEMENT.name: Risk of a material adjustment of carrying amounts next year
STR-EFFETS-AJUSTEMENT.definition: Qualitative and quantitative information on the risks and opportunities for which there is a significant risk of a material adjustment, within the next annual reporting period, to the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities of the financial statements (ESRS 2 §26, AR 16). Answer N/A if there is none.

STR-EFFETS-ATTENDUS.name: Anticipated financial effects of material risks and opportunities
STR-EFFETS-ATTENDUS.definition: Qualitative and quantitative information on how the financial position, financial performance and cash flows are expected to change over the short, medium and long term, given the strategy to manage the material risks and opportunities: investment and disposal plans, planned sources of funding (ESRS 2 §27, AR 17 to 21). Phase-in (ESRS 1 §125(b)-(c), §126(b)-(c), §127(b)-(c)): a wave-one company may omit this information for financial years before 2028 (quantitative information: before 2030); another company, for its first two financial years (quantitative information: first four).

STR-EFFETS-HORIZONS.name: Time horizons of the anticipated financial effects
STR-EFFETS-HORIZONS.definition: For each risk or opportunity, time horizon of the expected change: short term (the length of the financial statements period), medium term (from the end of the short term up to five years) or long term (more than five years), counted from the end of the reporting period (ESRS 2 §27; ESRS 1 §79). Phase-in (ESRS 1 §125(b)-(c), §126(b)-(c), §127(b)-(c)): a wave-one company may omit this information for financial years before 2028 (quantitative information: before 2030); another company, for its first two financial years (quantitative information: first four).

STR-EFFETS-SANS-CHIFFRES.name: Financial effects: why quantitative information is not given
STR-EFFETS-SANS-CHIFFRES.definition: Only if the company gives no quantitative information on the current or anticipated financial effects of a risk or opportunity (effects not separately identifiable, measurement uncertainty too high, or, for anticipated effects, lack of skills or resources): why (ESRS 2 §28, §29, §31(a)). Answer N/A otherwise.

STR-EFFETS-COMBINES.name: Financial effects not quantified: qualitative information and combined effects
